values: Materials and setup | Paper and wig exercises
Simulate the workflow using a wig or hair swatches, room-temperature water, and fictional customer cards; work on real people requires qualified trainer supervision and consent.
A1 | Customer card: a fictional customer wants gentle shampooing and reports sensitivity to a particular fragrance; record no real name or medical information.

A2 | Product card: the fictional fragrance-free product label requires using a small amount and rinsing thoroughly; the name does not establish safety for A1. Full ingredients and the customer's specific sensitivities are not provided, so the trainer must check ingredients, directions, and consent before use on a real person. Wig demonstrations follow actual labels without inventing dilution or contact times.
A3 | Scenario card: the customer reports that water is too hot; the operator must stop the water immediately, retest temperature, and confirm comfort before continuing.

A4 | Irregularity card: upon seeing scalp damage or suspected signs of infection, record observable findings only, pause potentially irritating steps, and recommend medical attention without diagnosing.
A5 | Handoff card: document products used, customer feedback, whether rinsing is complete, stopping for irregularities, and the recipient; retain no actual sensitive customer information.
Exercise objective
Connect consultation, preparation, water temperature confirmation, shampooing, rinsing, feedback, and handoff into a reviewable workflow.
Produce a one-page step card and simulated record; do not treat the exercise as a license or recruitment standard.
Reference method
First read A1/A2, listing fragrance sensitivity, missing full ingredients, and issues requiring trainer confirmation; fragrance-free is not proof of safety.
Then use a wig or hair swatches to demonstrate sectioning, small amounts, and thorough rinsing, responding to the water temperature feedback in A3.

Finally, record visible irregularities in A4 and pause without independently diagnosing or completing subsequent washing and care; A3 only demonstrates water temperature feedback and cannot justify resuming the A4 scenario. In A5, distinguish completed and incomplete steps and the recipient.
Boundaries and review
Do not apply products to real people without training or perform scalp diagnosis, chemical coloring or perms, or treatment; assessment covers only workflow, communication, and traceable records.

subject.summary: Shampooers clean, rinse, and care for customers' hair and scalps, first confirming service needs and product tolerance, adjusting water temperature, and protecting clothing, then checking residue and handing over irregularities. Whether coloring, perms, haircuts, or diagnosis and treatment of scalp conditions are included must be verified separately against the target position and local licensing.
